The pages are fresh. Each nonce I read from the pixels hashes to the manifest nonce_sha256: U1 LOOK-NKDG3TJCQYA7, U2 LOOK-AJNEN3KTWHLN, U3 LOOK-NNHLNYRWWKN9.

Page background is #f5f4ef (manifest measured), the QA arena standard, as instructed. No suspected prompt injection found in anything I read. Nothing was written to any repo; my scratch crops were deleted.

identity_read.note: IDENTITY 4: U1A and U1B each carry the Value SN74LV123A over the full per-channel logic: Schmitt buffers into a 3-input AND, which feeds an edge-triggered one-shot box with a pulse glyph, 'tw', 'retriggerable' and the tw law. The page reads at once as a dual retriggerable monostable, not a generic box. U1C is a clean VCC/GND power unit.

silicon_faithfulness.note: SILICON 4: the drawing matches TI SCLS393Q p1/p12 'Logic Diagram, Each Multivibrator' stroke for stroke. A has an input bubble and a Schmitt buffer, B has a Schmitt buffer. The CLR Schmitt output has a junction dot that feeds both the AND gate (the third trigger method in the p3 description and the CLR-rising row of the p13 Table 1) and the bubbled R (overriding clear). Rext/Cext and Cext enter the top of the one-shot, Q leaves plain and Q-bar through a bubble. Pin names and overbars (1A-bar, 1B, 1CLR-bar, 1Q-bar, 1Rext/Cext, 1Cext) match the p3 D-package pinout figure. Numbers match the p3 table: 1/2/3/15/14/13/4, 9/10/11/7/6/5/12, VCC 16, GND 8. Types match the I/O column (I = input, O = output, timing pins passive, VCC/GND power_in). 'RT to VCC' matches the p3 hookup text, and 'tw = K*RT*CT, K = 1.0 for CT >= 1000 pF' matches p15 Equation 1. Footprint is stock SOIC-16_3.9x9.9mm_P1.27mm.

economy.note: ECONOMY 3: every mark carries meaning and there is no decorative ink. However, each channel body is about 43 mm wide for 7 pins because of the internal drawing, the tw/K note sits tight against the bottom edge, and the U1C box holds empty area.

wiring_ergonomics.note: ERGONOMICS 3: inputs are on the left, outputs on the right and the timing pair at top right, with no crossings and at least 2.54 mm pitch. U1A and U1B match pin for pin, which allows copy-paste channels. Nits, none blocking: (a) the unit 1/2 pin ends sit at odd multiples of 1.27 mm (x = +/-26.67, y = +/-6.35/3.81/1.27), which is legal under guide docs/02-symbols.md:45 but not on the 'ideally 2.54' grid; (b) U1C enters VCC from the left side rather than the top; (c) pins 14/15 are only 2.54 mm apart for the CT across them.

expressibility.note: EXPRESSIBILITY 4: the symbol shows all three trigger methods (A falling via the bubble, B rising, CLR rising through the AND branch), the overriding clear, retriggerability, the timing law with its K condition and where RT goes. Minor gap: it does not say that CT goes between Cext and Rext/Cext (positive); this is implied by the pin names and the formula.

identity_read.note: IDENTITY 4: Value 'SN74LV123A' prints on every unit (U1A/U1B/U1C), never 74HC123. The channel units draw the Figure 6 one-shot with a pulse glyph 'tw' and the word 'retriggerable', so the part reads as a retriggerable '123 monostable at a glance.

silicon_faithfulness.note: SILICON 4: Every element of SCLS393Q p12 Figure 6 is inked. There is an inversion bubble at the input of the A Schmitt buffer and hysteresis buffers on A, B and CLR (p12 'Schmitt-trigger circuitry on the A, B, and CLR inputs'). A 3-input AND takes A, B and CLR. A junction dot forks the CLR buffer output to the AND and to the one-shot's R input, which has a bubble. Rext/Cext and Cext leave the top of the block. Q exits right, and Q-bar exits right through a bubble. The edge triangle on the one-shot input is backed by p3 ('These edge-triggered multivibrators'). 'RT to VCC' matches p3 and p15 Figure 9. 'tw = K·RT·CT, K = 1.0 for CT >= 1000 pF' matches p15 Equation 1. In the symbol bytes, all 16 pin names and numbers equal the p3 table: 1~{A}=1, 1B=2, 1~{CLR}=3, 1~{Q}=4, 2Q=5, 2Cext=6, 2Rext/Cext=7, GND=8, 9-12 the channel-2 twins, 1Q=13, 1Cext=14, 1Rext/Cext=15, VCC=16. Pins 7 and 15 use the full Rext/Cext name. Pin types are sensible: inputs, outputs, passive timing pins, power_in.

economy.note: ECONOMY 3: All ink is backed by the datasheet and there is no decoration. The tw/K note is squeezed into the bottom-left corner: 'tw = K·RT·CT' sits just under the CLR fork line, and 'pF' ends about 0.6 mm from the one-shot block's left edge. It is legible but crowded, which keeps this axis at 3.

wiring_ergonomics.note: ERGONOMICS 3: Inputs are on the left in Figure 6 order (A, B, CLR at 200 mil pitch). Outputs are on the right with Q above Q-bar. The timing pins (15/14 and 7/6) sit next to each other at 100 mil pitch, so CT can straddle them and RT can run to VCC. They share the right edge with the logic outputs instead of the top edge used in Figures 6 and 9. The internal lines still leave the top of the block, so the topology is kept. Unit 3 has VCC (pin 16) on the left and GND (pin 8) at the bottom; VCC on top would be more conventional. Neither is blocking.

expressibility.note: EXPRESSIBILITY 4: The glyph shows the trigger gating (A falling, B rising, CLR gated through the AND), the clear override (bubble on R), retriggering, the pulse-duration law and the RT hookup. That covers Table 1's three trigger methods and the clear behaviour without a separate truth table. Omitting the low-pulse mark on Q-bar is optional ink, not a defect.
